newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish tanker begins lifting Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: Turkish tanker begins lifting Iraqi oil.

text.p: The first tanker under the second term of Iraq's oil-for-food deal began lifting oil at Ceyhan at 2100 GMT on Wednesday, a Turkish pipeline official said.

"The lifting will take 39 hours, it started at midnight (2100 GMT). A total of 290,986 tonnes will be loaded in 39 hours. Its destination is the United States," Murat Demir, an official at the state pipeline company Botas, told Reuters.

Demir said the vessel, the Arcadia, was contracted by U.S. company Bayoil to load 2.1 million barrels as the first scheduled lifting of Iraqi Kirkuk oil under the second term of the U.N.-monitored oil-for-food deal which expires on December 8.
The Maltese-flagged Arcadia has been waiting off Ceyhan since Monday.
Iraq has to sell about 1.5 million barrels per day until September 5, when the first 90 days of the second six-month oil-for-food deal ends.
